sections.h2: Where to take a deed in Barry County
sections.html:
Go to Room 102 at the Barry County Courthouse, 220 W State Street, Hastings, MI 49058. The office is open Monday to Friday from 8:15 to 4:45, shuts for the noon hour, and answers at 269-945-1289 or bcrod@barrycounty.org. A recorded deed becomes public, but recording does not certify that the deed is legal.

Clerks record, index and preserve what arrives. They do not search titles, hand out blank forms or coach anyone on wording, so the deed itself comes from your closing agent or a lawyer. Nothing already on file can be altered, and a name added to or dropped from ownership means a brand-new deed gets signed and filed.

People sometimes ask for the "title" to a house. Most homes have none, since the recorded deed covers whatever is permanently fixed to the land. Certain mobile homes are the exception and may keep a separate title with the Secretary of State.

Before you go, call 269-945-1289 and ask what the packet needs. Bring the original deed, a check that covers the recording fee and the transfer tax, a second check for the treasurer's $5.00 certificate if the deed carries a warranty, and a stamped return envelope if you will not wait. Walk-in filers leave with the recorded copy the same day.

A flat $30.00 covers any document, and each added instrument number that a paper assigns or discharges brings another $3.00. Sale deeds and similar transfers owe state and county transfer tax on top, collected during recording. One payment to the Register of Deeds can cover the fee and the tax together.

One item travels separately. Land contracts, their assignments, warranty deeds and any deed with a warranty covenant require a Tax Certification from the Barry County Treasurer, priced at $5.00, written as its own check to the treasurer.

Barry County recording and copy charges

Recording a document$30.00
Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3.00

The counter takes cash, checks, and debit or credit cards; cards add a small service fee.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Barry County sale
sections.html:
The seller carries the tax, set at $4.30 for every $500 of consideration, with any partial block rounded up. It is due the moment the deed is recorded.

Some transfers escape the tax, though staff will not choose an exemption on your behalf. A deed claiming one must show MCL 207.505 (county) or MCL 207.526 (state) plus the exemption's letter, and the county posts separate lists for each. Have your closing agent make that call.

  • A gift deed to your child or grandchild is on the state's exempt list.
  • The state tax also skips foreclosure transfers and deeds given in place of foreclosure.
  • A corrective deed that only confirms what the grantee already owns is exempt, as is any paper priced under $100.

The full state list sits in MCL 207.526.

sections.h2: What a Barry County deed must include
sections.html:
State statutes set recording standards, and Barry posts a checklist drawn from them. Run through it before filing.

  • Ink signatures in black or dark blue, original rather than copied, with each name typed or printed under it.
  • An acknowledgment taken by a judge, a court clerk or a notary in Michigan, with the notary's name typed on the signature page.
  • A street or post office address for each grantee, and the drafter's name and address.
  • A blank 2.5 inch strip at the top of page one, and half an inch of white space around the rest.
  • Readable black print no smaller than 10 point, on white 20 pound paper sized from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14.
  • The property's full value stated in the deed, or a transfer tax valuation affidavit attached.
  • A certified death certificate recorded alongside, or ahead of, any deed that conveys by survivorship.

Photocopies are rejected. Court orders must carry the clerk's seal, and all other documents need original signatures.

sections.h2: Ways to file and when the paper comes back
sections.html:
You can carry the deed in, post it, or send it through an e-recording company. Barry names five: Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, Nationwide Title Clearing, EPN and CSC. A document sent by ordinary email is not recorded.

A paper that meets the standards is recorded the day it is received, and walk-in filers take the recorded copy home. Mail and drop-offs usually return in 2 to 4 business days. Enclose a stamped return envelope, or the office keeps the original for 90 days at least. Digital PDF returns through Swift are free and arranged with staff.

The treasurer issues electronic tax certifications only via Simplifile and CSC. Confirm that your closing agent's provider fits before signing day.

For an out-of-town seller, e-recording is usually the least trouble. The closing agent submits the signed deed, the provider forwards it to Hastings, and a PDF can come back by Swift at no charge. If you mail it instead, allow the 2 to 4 business days for return plus the time in the post.

Property tax is outside the register's job. Ask the city or township for current bills and the Barry County Treasurer for delinquent amounts. If the parcel has back tax, get a payoff figure from the treasurer first, so the closing agent can pay it from your proceeds.

Foreclosures reach the office only after the sale occurs, so staff cannot say whether a house is set for sheriff's sale. After a sheriff's deed is recorded, the office takes the redemption payment but does not compute it. Open liens show up in a title search, run at the public workstations or through a title firm.

For ownership questions, start with the county's GIS property map. It follows the tax roll and shows the listed taxpayer, while the recorded deed settles who actually owns the parcel.

sections.h2: Barry County housing at a glance
sections.html: Barry County's only city, Hastings, is also its seat. About 63,991 people lived here in 2025, in 24,480 households and 28,284 housing units. Owners occupy 87.3 percent of homes. Median value is $264,100 and median rent is $972. With a 27.7 minute average commute, drive time and condition both shape what buyers offer. Deferred repairs can block a mortgage, so some sellers turn to a cash buyer who will close as-is.

faqs.q: When is the Barry County deeds counter open?
faqs.a: Monday through Friday, 8:15 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., closed at noon for an hour. Phone 269-945-1289 before a long drive in case hours change.

faqs.q: Can I email a deed to Barry County for recording?
faqs.a: No. Plain email cannot be recorded. Send it through an approved provider such as Simplifile, EPN or CSC, or deliver the signed original.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for transfer tax in a Barry County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, and payment falls due at recording. The rate is $4.30 per $500, split as $3.75 to the state and $0.55 to the county.

faqs.q: Can Barry County staff tell me who owns a parcel?
faqs.a: Not directly. Staff can only retrieve the latest deed under a given name. Check the GIS property map for the listed taxpayer, then search that name at a public workstation.

faqs.q: How can I order a copy of a recorded Barry County deed?
faqs.a: The office will mail or email a copy at $1.00 a page, with a $5.00 search charge when you lack the document number. A check has to reach them first, because payment is not taken by email or phone.
